description: Migrate 150 production cron jobs from a fleet of 8 Linux servers to Apache Airflow. The cron jobs range from simple backup scripts to complex ETL pipelines with cross-job dependencies. The migration must follow: discover and inventory all cron jobs (crontab extraction, script dependency analysis), author Airflow DAGs (convert cron schedules to Airflow schedules, model dependencies as DAG edges), run a backfill parity check (run both cron and Airflow for a period, compare outputs), execute cutover (disable cron, enable Airflow as primary), verify, and retire cron jobs. A rollback plan must exist (re-enable cron, disable Airflow DAGs). Risk factors: hidden cron job dependencies (scripts that write to shared files), timezone differences between cron and Airflow, and backfill correctness. Tools available: Airflow, crontab, Python, cron-parser, Ansible, application logs.
